thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Region us-west-2 - sustained p99 latency > 2.5s and elevated 5xx rate across Hosted API and multiple Dedicated pools. Error traces show AWS STS 503/Throttling and CloudWatch/Kinesis PutRecords failures. Triage channel: #incidents. Paging oncall.

sam: seeing it in dashboards, p95/99 up, errors tagged STS::Throttling and cw:PutLogEventsFailure. Dedicated gpu-pool-3 has error spike. Confirmed by synthetic-canary failing.

maria: I'm oncall for infra, taking pager. starting triage. Can we confirm if this is regional? filter by region=us-west-2 -> yes.

josh: Dedicated-oncall here, popping into pools. Stack traces show token fetch delays from cred-proxy to STS, and our obs-forwarder to Kinesis timing out. Could be AWS control-plane or Kinesis shard throttling.

sam: rolling a temporary routing policy to route new hosted requests to eu-west-1 for non-data-residency customers: `routes update --region=us-west-2 --fallback=eu-west-1 --targets=hosted` (will start in 30s)

anna: I will notify support + CSMs: short customer impact: "Intermittent 5xx and elevated latency in us-west-2 since 14:12 UTC. We're routing to alternate region and investigating."

maria: running `aws sts get-caller-identity --region us-west-2` shows intermittent 503s and `ThrottlingException`. also Kinesis PutRecords errors: `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` from our obs stream. Filing AWS support ticket and opening AWS Health dashboard.

josh: mitigation: increase token cache TTL to 300s and enable local fallback path for cred-proxy: `kubectl set env deployment/cred-proxy TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=300` applied to us-west-2 clusters.

sam: applied routing fallback. metrics show 30% drop in 5xx for hosted after 90s. Dedicated pools still elevated for long-lived connections. Moving long requests to lower-priority queue.

lisa: about customers on Dedicated: switching to reduced batch size + backoff. `dedicated-pool update --pool=gpu-pool-3 --batch-size=1 --backoff=200ms` applied.

maria: AWS support responded: "We are investigating increased API throttling in us-west-2 for STS and Kinesis ingestion. No ETA yet." Adding oncall to the ticket.

josh: temporary per-pool fallback to model variant quantized-lt for lower latency: `runtime set-model --pool gpu-pool-3 --model quantized-lt --fallback=true` doing canary.

sam: customer comms updated: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1768004321 — note to CSMs: customers on Dedicated with pinned hosts may still see impact.

deploy-bot: Notify: Canary rollout for quantized-lt on gpu-pool-3 succeeded on 3/5 hosts. traffic cutover in progress.

anna: handoff to night oncall @maria in 30m. leaving notes in incident doc and Slack thread. If AWS publishes a regional fix, revert routing.

maria: ongoing: 1) AWS ticket open, 2) routing fallback active, 3) cred-proxy TTL increased, 4) pool batch/backoff reduced, 5) model fallback in progress. Next update in 15m or on significant change.

sam: :thumbsup: observed total 5xx down to baseline for hosted but dedicated slow drains. marking severity P2 -> keep pager open. will update when AWS resolves.

anna: adding postmortem owner @josh, assign action items: validate token backpressure mitigations, add regional runbook for auth-provider throttles, improve automatic fallback timings.

maria: AWS Health updated: "We have applied mitigations for STS and Kinesis in us-west-2; customers may see gradual recovery." Observability shows improving PutRecords success rate. will monitor for 1h.

sam: last: closing active pager handoff to oncall-night. if any regressions, reopen. Thanks all.
